macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks weakened as chip selloff offset falling oil prices
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.5%, the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.4% and the Dow rose 0.4% as weakness in chipmakers pressured technology shares. The Nasdaq 100 entered a technical correction, down 10% from its October peak, while crude oil prices fell amid hopes for diplomatic efforts related to the Iran war.

items.title: Oil prices plunged as markets assessed Iran diplomacy
items.summary: West Texas Intermediate settled near $96.50 a barrel after falling below $100, while Brent crude dropped sharply as Washington and Tehran signaled openness to talks. Lower energy prices eased immediate inflation concerns and supported bonds, with the 10-year Treasury yield near 4.90%.

items.title: Fed may reduce number of policy meetings in 2027
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is considering fewer rate-setting meetings next year, a change that could make each policy decision more consequential and increase market volatility around meeting dates.

items.title: Markets face a pivotal week of elections, earnings and jobs data
items.summary: Investors are preparing for U.S. midterm elections, Apple’s earnings report and October employment data. Markets are also pricing a high probability of a 25-basis-point Fed rate increase at the next policy meeting.

items.title: Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in major AI infrastructure deal
items.summary: Marvell Technology agreed to buy Lumentum Holdings at an enterprise value of about $115 billion, targeting demand for data-center networking and AI infrastructure. Marvell shares fell sharply after the announcement.

items.title: Anthropic disclosed sharp revenue growth and massive planned spending
items.summary: Anthropic reported a twelve-fold increase in quarterly revenue while indicating plans to spend more than $895 billion over coming years, highlighting both the scale of AI investment and growing investor concerns over capital intensity.

items.title: China announced additional market-support liquidity
items.summary: The People’s Bank of China said roughly 100 billion yuan, or about $15 billion, would be deployed through a new swap facility intended to provide financial firms with liquidity for market investment.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Binance resumes withdrawals after record hack
items.summary: Binance partially resumed withdrawals after a reported $6.3 billion theft attributed to the North Korean TraderTraitor group. The exchange said it would cover customer losses, while users withdrew a net $3.64 billion on the first day; Bitcoin traded near $78,000 and remained under pressure.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies remain volatile
items.summary: Bitcoin hovered around $77,000-$78,000 after falling about 7.5% in October. Ethereum traded near $2,250, while recent 24-hour movers included gains for Official Trump, Tron and Ethereum and declines for Basic Attention Token, NEAR Protocol and Theta Network.

items.title: Crypto investment products see renewed outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $202.6 million in weekly outflows, while spot Ethereum ETFs experienced a fifth consecutive week of withdrawals totaling about $431.5 million, adding to broader market caution.

items.title: FBI links Binance attack to North Korea
items.summary: The FBI reportedly attributed the Binance breach to the North Korean state-sponsored TraderTraitor group. Binance said it had frozen roughly $3 billion of affected assets and was using company funds to replace stolen customer holdings.

items.title: BTCPay warns of attacks on older installations
items.summary: BTCPay Server disclosed an attack vector affecting older versions of its Bitcoin payments software and urged users to update. Reports indicated that unauthorized attackers had drained some connected hot wallets.

items.title: Cardano advances Dijkstra-era development
items.summary: Intersect released Node 11.2 as a pre-release, providing Cardano developers with the Dijkstra-era feature set except for Leios. DijkstraNet and other test networks are being prepared for integration and testing ahead of broader adoption.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: CrowdStrike launches SafeMind AI security research effort
items.summary: CrowdStrike is pitting offensive AI models against simulated enterprise networks and using the resulting attack traces to train defensive models capable of autonomously hardening systems.

items.title: Anthropic reports rapid revenue growth while warning about autonomous AI development
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed sharply rising quarterly revenue in an IPO filing while continuing to report losses. The company also said it may revise its safety policy as AI increasingly contributes to the development of more capable models, while retaining meaningful human oversight.

items.title: Google DeepMind previews Genie 4 interactive world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind’s Genie 4 generates interactive environments in real time, adding native audio, dialogue, improved physics and more natural movement. The system is positioned for robotics simulation, AI-agent testing and research, but remains a limited preview.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate zero-data pretraining concept
items.summary: Researchers from Tel Aviv University and Stanford reported a preliminary proof of concept in which models trained only on self-generated data developed general predictive abilities across language, images, music, code and DNA. The results have so far been demonstrated only in relatively small models.

items.title: AI model reportedly identifies a Linux kernel vulnerability
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed a remote-root Linux kernel exploit reportedly discovered using an unreleased Claude model, highlighting the growing use of advanced AI systems for vulnerability research and the associated cybersecurity risks.

items.title: Companies expand enterprise AI infrastructure and security partnerships
items.summary: CrowdStrike and Dell announced an integrated security offering for Dell AI Factory infrastructure using NVIDIA computing, while Lumen and Microsoft expanded collaboration to connect enterprise data, applications and infrastructure for AI workloads.

items.title: Gartner warns of potential AI infrastructure impairment
items.summary: A report summarized by IT News Europe says Gartner estimates that more than $3.5 trillion in AI infrastructure spending could face impairment by 2030 and predicts consolidation among specialized cloud providers.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero sells 4 million copies in 72 hours
items.summary: S-Game’s action game Phantom Blade Zero reportedly sold more than 4 million copies within three days of its October 29 launch. Its Steam peak also reached 833,921 concurrent players on November 1.

items.title: Thief: The Dark Project Remastered launches December 3
items.summary: Atari, Nightdive Studios, and Eidos-Montréal announced a remaster of the classic stealth game for PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, Switch 2, and PC. It includes content from Thief: Gold, visual upgrades, and controller support.

items.title: Amazon plans to expand instant-play game demos
items.summary: Amazon is exploring distribution of browser-based, no-download game demos beyond Twitch. The initiative follows a Crimson Desert demo powered by Amazon GameLift Streams and could eventually support publisher demos across additional services and partner platforms.

items.title: Gravhounds joins Xbox Game Pass as a day-one November release
items.summary: The co-op action-builder Gravhounds entered Xbox Game Preview on November 2 and became the first day-one Xbox Game Pass addition announced for November 2026.

items.title: Sony Bend reportedly developing third-person co-op game
items.summary: Sony Bend is reportedly working on a third-person cooperative title that is not a live-service game or a Days Gone sequel. The project is reportedly planned for a 2027 reveal and release, though Sony has not officially announced it.

items.title: Steam releases nearly 1,900 games in one week
items.summary: Steam reportedly saw 1,879 games released between October 26 and November 1, highlighting the platform’s growing discoverability challenge for developers and players.

items.title: AI-generated game copycats raise developer concerns
items.summary: Developers are increasingly concerned about AI-assisted clones and low-quality AI-generated games appearing on digital storefronts. The issue became especially visible during Steam Next Fest, where some developers reportedly reconsidered releasing demos.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Supermarket freezers hit by apparent cyberattacks in Europe
items.summary: Supermarket freezer systems in several European countries were reportedly disrupted by apparent cyberattacks, affecting temperature-control operations and raising concerns about attacks on retail infrastructure.

items.title: Meta delays business terms after web-scraping backlash
items.summary: Meta postponed new terms for business accounts following criticism from media organizations and open-web advocates over provisions that could enable scraping of news websites.

items.title: Marvell announces acquisition of Lumentum
items.summary: Marvell Technology said it would acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal, combining suppliers of networking and optical components used in cloud infrastructure. Marvell shares fell sharply after the announcement, while Lumentum also declined.

items.title: IBM launches quantum-safe security software portfolio
items.summary: IBM unveiled a software portfolio designed to help organizations identify vulnerable encryption, monitor security risks, and transition to post-quantum cryptography before future quantum computers threaten current encryption standards.

items.title: Japanese online service company apologizes after security breaches
items.summary: GMO apologized for security breaches affecting its online services and said it would provide compensation, according to an Associated Press technology roundup.

items.title: Mexico bans cellphones in schools
items.summary: Mexico introduced a school cellphone ban despite opposition from some parents who cited concerns about student safety and communication during emergencies.
